entries.proposition: Untreated wild-type littermates had no atypical absence seizures (0 of 6) while all knock-in mice had them (7 of 7). The wild-type arm is at an absolute zero baseline for this endpoint.
entries.snippet: No WT (0/6) and all KI animals (7/7) displayed atypical absence seizures (mean ± SEM 7.4 ± 3.1; range 1–21)

entries.proposition: The drug experiments were run in knock-in mice only. The crossover design is vehicle versus drug within the same mutant animal; wild-type mice were not dosed on the seizure endpoint, so the paper has no wild-type drug arm and cannot separate knock-in from wild-type drug response. The selection row's phrase 'separate KI from wild-type littermates in a within-subject crossover' is not what the Methods describe.
entries.snippet: KI mice were randomized to treatment order using a Latin‐square design with a one‐week washout period between experiments.

entries.proposition: Ethosuximide reduced cumulative atypical absence seizure incidence by about two thirds in the mutant, paired within animal (n = 9).
entries.snippet: reduced total seizure incidence by 64% (vehicle 21.4 ± 4.7, range 5–45 vs. ethosuximide 7.7 ± 1.8, range 1–20; t(8) = 2.6, p = 0.03)
entries.anchor: Results, Antiseizure drugs reduce atypical absence seizures

entries.proposition: A Cav3-selective inhibitor (ulixacaltamide) produced the same size of reduction in seizure incidence as ethosuximide in this knock-in (about 64 percent, n = 11), in a different compound class. The two were given in separate cohorts and the paper does not compare them statistically.
entries.snippet: reduced total seizure incidence by 64% (vehicle 21.1 ± 2.8, range 5–44 vs. ulixacaltamide 7.5 ± 2.3, range 0–22; t(10) = 3.5, p = 0.006)
entries.anchor: Results, Antiseizure drugs reduce atypical absence seizures

entries.proposition: The authors treat ethosuximide as primarily Cav3-acting with additional Cav1, sodium and potassium actions, and use ulixacaltamide to isolate Cav3. Their inference that Cav3 channels are rational targets rests on the compound agreement, with no channel measurement in the model.
entries.snippet: While its primary mechanism involves Cav3 inhibition, it also modulates Cav1, sodium, and potassium conductances.

entries.proposition: Injection stress is a stated confound: vehicle-treated knock-in animals had markedly more seizures (about 21 per hour, vehicle rows) than the uninjected animals of Figure 1 (about 7), and the authors suggest the procedure itself may precipitate seizures. Any effect of a drug versus vehicle in an injected mutant is measured on an injection-elevated baseline.
entries.snippet: suggesting that procedural stress associated with intraperitoneal injections may precipitate seizures in Gabrb3 +/D120N mice.

entries.proposition: Figure 1B read as an image: six wild-type circles all at zero events and seven knock-in dots from about 1 to about 21 (bar about 7.4); panels C and E show wild type flat at zero across all six 10 min bins.

entries.proposition: Figure 2A read as an image (ethosuximide): nine paired animals; eight fall, one rises from about 9 to about 20; vehicle bar about 21, drug bar about 8. Figure 2B: vehicle incidence per 10 min bin rises from about 2 to about 4.4 across the hour while drug stays about 0.5 to about 2.3, with stars at 10 to 50 min. The drug effect is clear but not complete, and not uniform across animals.

entries.proposition: Spasm arm: a subset of wild-type pups also showed spasm-like events (4 of 11) against all knock-in pups (10 of 10), and only knock-in pups were allocated to drug or vehicle. The wild-type spasm floor is above zero, and the paper says its spasm scoring is behavioural without EEG confirmation and not controlled for sedation.
entries.snippet: To assess sensitivity to ASMs, KI pups were randomly allocated to receive vigabatrin, CBD, or vehicle.

Treated knock-in values stay above the wild-type mean.
